description: Co-funds the costs of bringing in foreign specialists to train local workers, or sending locals overseas to acquire niche skills.
fundingamount: Salary support ranging from 30% to 90%, plus co-funding for foreign specialist airfare and accommodation.
eligibilitycriteria: Registered/operating in SG; projects must clearly transfer niche capabilities that do not currently exist in the local workforce.
supportedusecases: Bringing a German precision engineering master craftsman to train SG staff; sending SG biotech researchers to the US for training.
applicationprocess: 1. Draft capability transfer plan. 2. Submit application via WSG portal. 3. Conduct training. 4. Claim based on achieved training outcomes.
requireddocuments: Detailed OJT/training syllabus, CVs of foreign specialists and local trainees, cost breakdown.
restrictionsnotes: Cannot be used for generic training; the skill sets must be highly specialized and scarce in the Singaporean labour market.

description: Helps SMEs adopt digital solutions
fundingamount: Varies (often PSG-linked)
eligibilitycriteria: SG SMEs
supportedusecases: Digital transformation
applicationprocess: Select solution ? apply via PSG/BGP
requireddocuments: Vendor docs
restrictionsnotes: Sector-specific

description: Supports local hiring
fundingamount: Salary support (time-bound)
eligibilitycriteria: Employers hiring locals
supportedusecases: Hiring expansion
applicationprocess: Auto-assessed
requireddocuments: CPF records
restrictionsnotes: Time-limited scheme

description: Helps Singapore SMEs expand into new overseas markets by defraying costs of market promotion, business development, and set-up. Each application covers one activity in one overseas market.
fundingamount: Up to 70% of eligible costs (effective 1 Apr 2026 per Budget 2026); capped at S$100,000 per company per new market: Promotion S$20K cap + BD S$50K cap + Set-Up S$30K cap
eligibilitycriteria: ① Registered & operating in Singapore ② ?30% local equity ③ Group turnover ?S$100M OR ?200 employees ④ Annual sales in target market must not have exceeded S$100,000 in any of the past 3 years
supportedusecases: Overseas marketing/PR campaigns, trade fair participation, identifying partners/distributors, in-market BD services, deploying BD staff overseas, market entry advisory (IP filing, incorporation, import/export licensing)
applicationprocess: 1. Confirm target market sales history <S$100K in past 3 years 2. Identify activity type (Promotion/BD/Set-Up) 3. Obtain quotes 4. Submit application via BGP at least 6 months before project start 5. Await LOF 6. Execute activity 7. Submit claim with supporting docs
requireddocuments: Market research report; vendor quotes; travel itinerary; proof of market entry activity; invoices and receipts
restrictionsnotes: One application per market per activity type. Cannot apply <6 months before project start. Retrospective applications rejected. Eligible for additional SFEC subsidies. Third-party agents cannot apply on behalf of companies.

description: Supports sustainability capability building
fundingamount: Subsidised training
eligibilitycriteria: SG SMEs
supportedusecases: Sustainability transformation
applicationprocess: Apply via EnterpriseSG
requireddocuments: Participation records
restrictionsnotes: Programme-based

description: Encourages research and innovation in land transport technologies to solve mobility challenges.
fundingamount: Up to 70% of qualifying project costs
eligibilitycriteria: Companies, startups, or research institutes registered in SG.
supportedusecases: Autonomous vehicles research, smart traffic management systems, active mobility tech.
applicationprocess: Submit proposal to LTA > Technical evaluation > Grant award.
requireddocuments: Technical blueprint, Proof of scalability, Budget overview.
restrictionsnotes: Project must address LTA's strategic goals (e.g., reducing carbon emissions, easing congestion).

description: Enables SMEs to participate in pre-approved B2B and B2C global e-commerce platforms to reach overseas markets.
fundingamount: Up to 70% funding on the platform subscription and associated setup costs.
eligibilitycriteria: Registered/operating in SG; at least 30% local shareholding; SME criteria.
supportedusecases: Listing on global B2C marketplaces (e.g., Amazon, Shopee) or B2B platforms, integrating e-payment, digital marketing setup.
applicationprocess: 1. Choose a pre-approved platform. 2. Contact platform vendor. 3. Apply on BGP. 4. Launch and claim.
requireddocuments: Vendor quote, ACRA Bizfile, financial statements.
restrictionsnotes: Must be a new subscriber to the specific platform. Does not cover inventory or ad-spend directly.

description: Supports Singapore companies in upgrading capabilities, innovating, and expanding overseas. Funds customised projects across three pillars: Core Capabilities, Innovation & Productivity, and Market Access.
fundingamount: Up to 50% of eligible costs (consultancy, software/equipment, manpower); up to 70% for sustainability-related projects
eligibilitycriteria: ① Registered & operating in Singapore ② ?30% local equity ③ Group turnover ?S$100M OR ?200 employees ④ Project must be new, not yet revenue-generating ⑤ No contracts/work commenced before application
supportedusecases: Business strategy, financial management, HR, branding, process redesign, automation, product development, overseas expansion, sustainability, IP management, standards adoption
applicationprocess: 1. Identify project pillar 2. Engage SAC-accredited consultant (TR43/SS680 for consultancy costs) 3. Prepare proposal + 3-year financial projections 4. Submit on BGP 5. Await assessment 6. Accept LOF 7. Complete project 8. Submit claim with auditor within 6 months of project end
requireddocuments: Project proposal; 3-year financial projections (revenue, staff remuneration, depreciation, NOPBT); consultant credentials; quotations
restrictionsnotes: No pre-approved vendors. Reimbursement basis. Auditor required for claims (up to S$500 or 70% of audit fee covered). No compulsory application fees � third-party agents quoting fees are NOT endorsed by EnterpriseSG.

description: Incentivises employers to commit to part-time re-employment policies for senior workers to encourage flexible workforce planning.
fundingamount: Up to S$125,000 per enterprise (up to S$2,500 per eligible senior worker placed on part-time re-employment).
eligibilitycriteria: Registered/operating in SG; legally binding flexible work and part-time re-employment policies published in employee handbooks.
supportedusecases: Transitioning staff aged 60+ to 3-day work weeks, retaining institutional knowledge via flexible mentoring roles.
applicationprocess: 1. Update HR policy to formalize part-time re-employment. 2. Apply via WSG portal. 3. Submit claims based on senior worker headcount.
requireddocuments: Updated HR policy handbook, ACRA Bizfile, senior employee contracts and CPF records.
restrictionsnotes: Company must officially sign onto the Tripartite Standard on Flexible Work Arrangements to qualify.

description: Supports digital transformation leaders
fundingamount: Co-funding varies
eligibilitycriteria: High-growth SMEs
supportedusecases: Digital strategy, leadership
applicationprocess: Apply via IMDA
requireddocuments: Business roadmap
restrictionsnotes: Selective entry

description: Supports tourism businesses to adopt technology, improve business processes, and develop innovative solutions to increase productivity and competitiveness. Covers both SME tourism businesses and tech companies creating products for tourism.
fundingamount: Up to 70% for SMEs; up to 50% for non-SMEs. Covers consultancy fees, hardware, software, equipment, training, travel, and sustainability certification costs.
eligibilitycriteria: ① Singapore-registered company in the tourism sector (hotels, travel agencies, attractions, MICE, lifestyle businesses) OR tech companies creating innovative products/services for tourism ② Hotels/hostels must hold valid HLB licence ③ SME: ?30% local equity, turnover ?S$100M OR ?200 employees ④ Project must not have commenced before application
supportedusecases: Technology innovation for tourism, process redesign, service excellence, sustainability certification, capability development, productivity improvement, new tourism product development
applicationprocess: 1. Prepare executive summary (project objectives, description, schedule, costing) 2. Email STB_Incentives@stb.gov.sg for pre-assessment 3. STB advises on eligibility 4. Submit formal application via BGP with Corppass 5. Processing up to 90 days 6. Accept LOF 7. Complete project 8. Submit AUP Report + claim
requireddocuments: Executive summary; detailed project proposal; financial statements; quotations from vendors; Agreed-Upon Procedures (AUP) Report by practitioner for disbursement
restrictionsnotes: No retrospective applications. Projects must not have commenced before application. Reimbursement basis. AUP Report required before disbursement. Contact STB_Incentives@stb.gov.sg for enquiries.

description: Helps Singapore SMEs adopt pre-approved IT solutions, equipment, and consultancy services to improve productivity and automate processes. Covers generic (all sectors) and sector-specific solutions.
fundingamount: Up to 50% of eligible costs; annual cap of S$30000 per company (per 1 Apr–31 Mar cycle)
eligibilitycriteria: ① Registered & operating in Singapore ② ?30% local equity (SC/PR ultimate ownership) ③ Group turnover ?S$100M OR ?200 employees ④ Solution used in Singapore ⑤ No payment/contract with vendor before application
supportedusecases: Accounting software, HR/payroll systems, CRM, inventory management, POS systems, cybersecurity, digital marketing tools, sector-specific equipment (F&B, retail, manufacturing)
applicationprocess: 1. Browse pre-approved solutions on GoBusiness Gov Assist 2. Get vendor quotation 3. Submit on BGP via Corppass 4. Await LOF (~4–6 weeks) 5. Accept LOF 6. Pay vendor 7. Submit reimbursement claim on BGP
requireddocuments: Vendor quotation (matching Annex 3 of PSG package); Corppass account
restrictionsnotes: Charities, IPCs, VWOs, government agencies excluded. Retrospective applications not allowed. Reimbursement basis. Do not share Corppass with vendors. Annual cap resets every 1 Apr.

description: Supports industry associations
fundingamount: Co-funding varies
eligibilitycriteria: Trade associations
supportedusecases: Industry capability building
applicationprocess: Apply via EnterpriseSG
requireddocuments: Project proposal
restrictionsnotes: Association-focused

description: Helps organisations with Company Training Committees (CTCs) implement transformation plans that improve both business capabilities and worker outcomes simultaneously. S$200M committed by government.
fundingamount: Funding quantum varies by project scope. Covers costs of transformation plans including training, job redesign, and technology adoption. S$200M top-up announced at Budget 2025; now covers employer-led training leading to formal qualifications.
eligibilitycriteria: ① Must have formed a Company Training Committee (CTC) ② Singapore-registered employer ③ Project must deliver both enterprise transformation AND workforce transformation outcomes ④ Must commit to at least 1 workforce outcome (e.g. wage increase, job redesign, new career pathway)
supportedusecases: Digitalisation, productivity improvement, innovation, job redesign, workforce reskilling, career development, formal qualification attainment for workers
applicationprocess: 1. Engage e2i to review draft transformation plan (e2i.sg/ctcenquiries) 2. Prepare transformation and training plan 3. Submit via e2i Grant Portal (online only; no email/hardcopy) 4. Receive Letter of Award (LOA) 5. Implement project 6. Submit claim within 4 weeks after project end
requireddocuments: Transformation plan; training plan; senior management representative sign-off; worker outcome commitments; supporting cost invoices
restrictionsnotes: Open for applications 1 Aug 2022 – 31 Jul 2026. Unionised companies: engage union/U SME rep. Non-unionised: contact e2i at e2i.sg/ctcenquiries. Multiple applications allowed if each covers new scope. Claims must be filed within 4 weeks after project end.

description: Supports the creation of a vibrant ecosystem for innovation in the financial sector.
fundingamount: Up to 50% - 70% of qualifying costs depending on the track
eligibilitycriteria: Financial institutions or FinTech firms registered and operating in SG.
supportedusecases: Innovation labs, early-stage deep-tech in finance, ESG FinTech solutions, AI risk management.
applicationprocess: Submit proposal to MAS > Technical review > Grant offer > Milestone-based claims.
requireddocuments: Technical architecture, Business case, Financial projections.
restrictionsnotes: Solutions must explicitly benefit the Singapore financial sector.

description: Encourages technology adoption, innovation, and job redesign specifically for businesses in the tourism sector.
fundingamount: Up to 70% of qualifying costs for SMEs (up to 50% for non-SMEs) covering consultancy, software, and training.
eligibilitycriteria: Tourism-related companies (hotels, travel agents, tourist guides, MICE organizers) registered/operating in SG.
supportedusecases: Implementing contactless hotel check-in kiosks, automating travel agency ticketing, MICE event digital platforms.
applicationprocess: 1. Submit pre-application executive summary. 2. Full application via BGP. 3. Execute project. 4. Final audit and claim.
requireddocuments: Executive summary, detailed project proposal, vendor quotations, audited financial statements.
restrictionsnotes: Functions identically to the EDG but is ringfenced and evaluated specifically by STB for tourism impact.

description: Supports overseas innovation partnerships
fundingamount: Co-funding varies
eligibilitycriteria: SG companies
supportedusecases: Innovation, partnerships
applicationprocess: Apply via EnterpriseSG
requireddocuments: Project proposal
restrictionsnotes: Partner network required

description: Supports the early adoption of advanced, highly integrated digital and sustainability pilot solutions.
fundingamount: Up to 70% funding for qualifying costs including hardware, software, integration, and project management.
eligibilitycriteria: Registered/operating in SG; minimum 30% local equity; SME scale (turnover <S$100M OR <200 employees); project must be new and not yet revenue-generating.
supportedusecases: AI/ML pilots, IoT integration, blockchain proof-of-concept, advanced robotics, sustainability tech pilots.
applicationprocess: 1. Identify advanced solution 2. Engage vendor 3. Submit application via BGP 4. Await assessment 5. Accept LOF 6. Implement pilot 7. Submit claim
requireddocuments: Project proposal, Technical architecture, Vendor quotations, Financial projections
restrictionsnotes: Solutions must be advanced/emerging tech. Standard IT solutions should use PSG instead.

grantname: MAS Artificial Intelligence and Data Analytics Grant
description: Supports financial institutions and fintech companies to implement AI and data analytics (AIDA) solutions for business innovation, risk management, and customer service improvement in the financial sector.
fundingamount: Up to 50% of qualifying costs (exact quantum varies by project scope and type � verify with MAS directly)
eligibilitycriteria: ① Financial institution or fintech company licensed/regulated by MAS OR company providing financial services ② Singapore-registered entity ③ Project must involve genuine AIDA adoption for the financial sector
supportedusecases: AI/ML for financial services, data analytics, credit risk modelling, fraud detection, personalised financial services, regulatory compliance automation, fintech innovation
applicationprocess: 1. Prepare project proposal with AIDA use case 2. Submit to MAS for evaluation 3. Await assessment and LOF 4. Implement project 5. Submit claim with supporting evidence
requireddocuments: Project proposal; cost breakdown; technical documentation; team credentials; evidence of AIDA solution viability
restrictionsnotes: Financial sector specific (MAS-regulated entities and fintech). Verify current quantum and eligibility directly with MAS as scheme parameters may be updated.

description: Provides funding to SG enterprises offering student internships and management associate programs to build a talent pipeline.
fundingamount: Up to 70% funding support on the monthly internship stipend or management trainee starting salary.
eligibilitycriteria: Registered/operating in SG; at least 30% local shareholding; active HR policies; financially viable.
supportedusecases: Hiring ITE/Polytechnic/University students for tech, marketing, or engineering internships; Overseas MT postings.
applicationprocess: 1. Apply to be an approved GRT employer via portal. 2. Post job openings. 3. Hire student. 4. Submit claims post-internship.
requireddocuments: Internship training plan, student matriculation proof, employment contract, payroll evidence.
restrictionsnotes: Internships must offer substantive learning experiences; routine clerical or purely manual labour roles are excluded.

description: Supports projects that enhance productivity, innovation, and sustainability in Singapore's aviation sector.
fundingamount: Up to 70% of qualifying costs for approved projects.
eligibilitycriteria: Companies operating in Singapore's aviation sector (airlines, MRO, ground handlers, cargo operators, airport tenants at Changi/Seletar).
supportedusecases: Automation of ground handling, MRO process innovation, sustainable aviation fuel trials, digital twin for aircraft maintenance.
applicationprocess: 1. Prepare project proposal 2. Submit to CAAS 3. Technical evaluation 4. Approval 5. Execute project 6. Claim reimbursement
requireddocuments: Project proposal, Cost-benefit analysis to the aviation sector.
restrictionsnotes: Must demonstrate direct productivity improvements at Changi or Seletar airport ecosystems.

description: Provides wage offsets to employers who hire Singapore Citizen workers aged 55 and above and earning below S$4,000/month, to encourage employment of senior workers. Extended until 2026.
fundingamount: Up to 8% of monthly wages for employees aged 60–64; up to 7% for aged 55–59 (rates vary by age band and year). Exact percentages vary � verify with IRAS.
eligibilitycriteria: ① Singapore-registered employer ② Hired Singapore Citizen aged ?55 earning <S$4,000/month ③ Employee must be making CPF contributions
supportedusecases: Hiring senior workers for any role, retaining experienced staff, workforce age diversity
applicationprocess: Automatic assessment by IRAS based on CPF records. No application required. Credit paid directly to employer.
requireddocuments: None (automatic via CPF contribution records)
restrictionsnotes: Automatic scheme. Does not apply to business owners. Rates and caps vary by year � verify current rates with IRAS.

description: Helps SMEs better recruit, train, manage, and retain newly-hired PMETs.
fundingamount: One-off grant of $5,000
eligibilitycriteria: SMEs registered in SG, offering gross monthly salary of at least $2,500 to the PMET.
supportedusecases: HR framework implementation, onboarding training for new PMET hires.
applicationprocess: Register with Programme Manager > PMET and Supervisor attend workshop > Retain PMET for 6 months > Claim.
requireddocuments: Employment contract, Workshop attendance proof.
restrictionsnotes: PMET must be retained for at least 6 months after the workshop.

description: Facilitates the growth of SG's maritime cluster by funding manpower development, business development, and tech adoption.
fundingamount: Up to 50%-70% co-funding for short courses, certs, overseas BD trips, and sustainability tech adoption in maritime.
eligibilitycriteria: Registered in SG; core business in maritime (shipping, port ops, marine tech).
supportedusecases: Decarbonisation tech for vessels, staff attending advanced maritime logistics courses, establishing new maritime tech offices.
applicationprocess: 1. Submit application to MPA prior to project/course start. 2. Receive Letter of Offer. 3. Complete project. 4. Submit claim.
requireddocuments: Course/project details, vendor/trainer quotes, company profile, financial health proof.
restrictionsnotes: Activities must demonstrably enhance Singapore's position as an International Maritime Centre (IMC).

description: Co-funds investments in energy-efficient equipment to reduce electricity/energy costs and carbon emissions.
fundingamount: Base Tier: Up to 70% for SMEs (capped at S$30k). Advanced Tier: Up to S$350,000 based on lifetime carbon savings.
eligibilitycriteria: Registered/operating in SG; at least 30% local equity; sector-specific criteria (expanded to all sectors in 2026).
supportedusecases: Replacing legacy air-conditioning, chillers, LED lighting, or deploying high-efficiency industrial motors/equipment.
applicationprocess: 1. Assess equipment via pre-approved list. 2. Obtain quotes. 3. Apply via BGP. 4. Install and submit claims.
requireddocuments: Energy audit/specs, vendor quotations, ACRA Bizfile, site utility bills.
restrictionsnotes: Equipment must be used in Singapore and kept operational for at least one year.

description: Tax incentive allowing companies to claim 200% tax deduction on qualifying overseas market expansion and investment development expenses, without prior approval for standard activities under Sections 14B/14H/14I of the Income Tax Act 1947.
fundingamount: 200% tax deduction on qualifying expenses (up to specified expenditure caps per activity; pre-approval from ESG or STB required for amounts above caps or for non-standard activities)
eligibilitycriteria: ① Singapore tax-resident company ② Expenses incurred in qualifying activities ③ Must maintain documentation as proof of expenditure and purpose ④ Additional activities (e-commerce campaigns from 15 Feb 2023) also qualify
supportedusecases: Overseas market promotion, trade fairs, overseas investment study trips, product/service advertising overseas, E-commerce campaigns (new from 15 Feb 2023), market research, FTA/trade compliance activities
applicationprocess: 1. Incur qualifying expenses 2. Maintain supporting documentation 3. Standard activities: no prior approval needed � claim via IRAS tax filing 4. Non-standard/above-cap activities: apply to ESG or STB for case-by-case approval 5. Submit documentation upon IRAS request
requireddocuments: Expenditure records; invoices; purpose documentation; for above-cap/non-standard activities: approval letter from ESG or STB
restrictionsnotes: Not a cash grant � a tax deduction. Cap applies per activity without pre-approval. IRAS may request documentation audit. E-commerce campaign activity added 15 Feb 2023.

description: Co-funds wage increases given to lower-wage resident employees to help employers manage costs.
fundingamount: Up to 50% co-funding for wage increases
eligibilitycriteria: Employers who give qualifying wage increases to resident employees earning up to $3,000/month.
supportedusecases: General operational support, offsetting salary increment costs to retain lower-wage staff.
applicationprocess: Automatically disbursed by IRAS based on CPF contribution data. No application required.
requireddocuments: None (computed automatically via CPF).
restrictionsnotes: Does not apply to business owners or their spouses.

grantname: Enterprise Financing Scheme SME Working Capital Loan
agency: Enterprise Singapore (ESG) via participating financial institutions
description: Provides Singapore SMEs with easier access to working capital loans to support daily operational cash flow needs. Government shares loan default risk with participating financial institutions.
fundingamount: Loan quantum up to S$500,000; tenure up to 5 years. Government risk-share: up to 70% (SMEs). Interest rates set by participating banks.
eligibilitycriteria: ① Singapore-registered and operating business ② ?30% local equity ③ Group turnover ?S$100M OR ?200 employees ④ Financially viable with ability to service loan
supportedusecases: Daily operational cash flow, short-term working capital needs, business continuity, bridging cash flow gaps, operational expenses
applicationprocess: 1. Approach any participating financial institution (DBS, UOB, OCBC, etc.) 2. Submit loan application with required documents 3. Bank assesses creditworthiness 4. Loan disbursed if approved
requireddocuments: Business financial statements; ACRA bizfile; bank statements; business plan (bank-specific requirements vary)
restrictionsnotes: Not a grant � a loan with government risk-share. Repayment required. Interest rates vary by bank. Part of broader Enterprise Financing Scheme (EFS) which also covers Trade Loans, Green Loans, Fixed Assets Loans, and M&A Loans.

description: Co-funds salary costs when companies hire and reskill mid-career workers into new roles. Operates via Place-and-Train (hire first then train) and Attach-and-Train (train at host company first) models, managed by approved programme managers.
fundingamount: Up to 90% of monthly salary support during retraining period for mature workers (?40 yrs) or long-term unemployed; up to 70% for other eligible hires. Duration varies by programme. From 1 Apr 2025: flexi-load (part-time) arrangements also supported.
eligibilitycriteria: ① Registered employer in Singapore ② Hiring Singapore Citizens or PRs ③ Worker must be a mid-career switcher into a new occupation ④ Role must be on WSG-approved CCP occupation list ⑤ Employer must commit to retaining employee post-training
supportedusecases: Digital roles, tech/ICT, finance, sustainability, professional services, new job roles created by industry transformation, career switches into growth sectors
applicationprocess: 1. Identify approved CCP programme for target occupation 2. Contact programme manager or WSG 3. Submit application via programme manager 4. Hire/attach candidate 5. Undergo structured OJT retraining 6. Claim salary support
requireddocuments: Employment contract; training plan; proof of new occupation; salary records; relevant WSG-required forms per programme
restrictionsnotes: Funding rate varies by programme, employer profile, and worker demographics. List of approved occupations varies. From 1 Apr 2025 part-time arrangements also qualify.
